title: Solo-Founder Market Research: Failure Traps vs. Solutions
subtitle: Lessons from 19 Reddit threads and 152 retrieved comment bodies; incomplete coverage and unverified practitioner accounts

trap.title: Research Without a Decision
trap.description: Collecting interesting information without knowing which business choice it should change.

solution.title: Decision-First Brief
solution.description: Define the decision, risky assumption, disconfirming evidence, cost of being wrong, and research budget before collecting data.

trap.title: The Attractive Market Report
trap.description: Treating market growth or a large category estimate as proof that reachable customers will buy your product.

solution.title: Named Buyers and Buying Signals
solution.description: Identify active accounts, relevant workflows, budget owners, ownership groups, and contact routes. Use reports as context, not purchase evidence.

trap.title: Asking for Idea Approval
trap.description: Asking whether people like your idea or can name problems, then treating positive reactions as validation.

solution.title: Recent Workflow Walkthroughs
solution.description: Investigate actual tasks, exceptions, workarounds, costs, and buying authority. Include people outside your network and those happy with existing solutions.

trap.title: Disguised or Generic Recruitment
trap.description: Posting AI-written research requests, hiding commercial intent, or ignoring community rules.

solution.title: Honest, Specific Outreach
solution.description: Explain your affiliation, audience fit, time commitment, and purpose in your own words. Seek permission and offer appropriate compensation for time.

trap.title: Pricing Before Audience Fit
trap.description: Testing prices on people who like the story but do not buy the category, or have money but no reason to switch.

solution.title: Buyer Fit, Then a Real Offer
solution.description: Identify category buyers and competing uses of budget. Refine a price hypothesis, then test a scoped paid pilot or transparent preorder with qualified prospects.

trap.title: The Magic Sample Size
trap.description: Assuming a response count guarantees representativeness or that preference, usefulness, and purchase intent are interchangeable.

solution.title: Match Method to the Question
solution.description: Separate workflow discovery, prevalence estimation, and offer testing. Keep wording and context controlled; label directional findings and sampling limits.

trap.title: AI-Generated Validation
trap.description: Using synthetic respondents or unchecked summaries as evidence of real demand and willingness to pay.

solution.title: AI Assistance with Traceable Sources
solution.description: Use AI to rehearse guides, organize real notes, and draft reproducible analysis. Verify claims and calculations; keep generated hypotheses separate from observations.

trap.title: Evergreen Findings
trap.description: Reusing old quotes without dates or trusting plausible numbers after unexplained data transformations.

solution.title: Evidence Log and Targeted Refresh
solution.description: Record source, date, segment, uncertainty, decision, and refresh trigger. Recheck affected assumptions after changes and reconcile important data handoffs.
